purpose: Seek a material pricing or hedging improvement, without claiming a new mathematical method merely for combining established components.
development: Previously examined 2020 six-name dataset; all results from it remain development results.
pricing_candidates: Reference-IV PCHIP, linear IV, butterfly-constrained SSVI; convex natural-cubic call-price projection with linear-IV, PCHIP or structural-residual hybrid prior, weights 0.1, 1, 10. Common reference/target contracts. Within-expiry constraints only; no cross-expiry no-arbitrage claim.
pricing_selection: Among candidates with at least 99.9% solver and strike-grid validity, select smallest equally weighted snapshot MAE on 2020. Benchmark against all three interpolation/SSVI alternatives and the same constrained smoother without structural information. Keep all failures in coverage; do not silently remove them.
risk_candidates: Reference-contract past-only ridge regression: published Hull-White-style delta/vega features as benchmark; add structural delta gap and fitted event-variance fraction interactions as candidates. Black-Scholes and structural deltas also reported. Evaluate withheld contracts; train only on reference-contract outcomes realized strictly before the scoring close.
risk_training: Rolling past 120 calendar days, minimum 30 distinct completed dates. Equal total training weight per issuer/date; ridge 0.01 on standardized design. No outcome clipping. Bound effective call delta to [0,1] and put delta to [-1,0] identically for learned models.
historical_confirmation: After development, freeze selected pricing and hedge specifications before inspecting a new 2025 option-quote evaluation panel. Calendar metadata may be retrospective, so do not call this a prospectively untouched trading test. Preserve reserved October 2026–March 2027 prospective window.
success: On historical confirmation, at least 5% lower primary loss than the strongest applicable simpler benchmark; paired calendar-week interval supports improvement; improvement is not attributable to one issuer; disclose consistency failures, tail risk and coverage. For pricing use equal-snapshot MAE; for hedging use equal-snapshot mean squared error plus absolute-error and tail diagnostics. No trading alpha claim from either metric alone.
novelty: Maintain prior-art map. Constrained splines, SSVI, scheduled jumps and empirical minimum-variance hedging are established. Any originality claim needs a specifically identified difference and further literature review.
